text:
support-ops: @here CS flagged a customer escalation (GammaApps) — they report lots of 5xx and timeouts hitting the hosted inference API since ~2026-03-15T14:10Z. SLO alerts triggered: /v1/generate latency +5xx. Customer is seeing intermittent failures and billing anomalies. Repro shown below. Can SRE take a look? :sadpanda:

maria: I’m on it. Do we have the alert link and which region?

support-ops: Alert: <https://grafana.redwood.io/d/alerts/ALERT-1234> — region us-west-2, route /v1/generate. Alert payload: slo_burn=4.2, 5xx_rate=0.9r/s (5m). Customer provided a curl repro: 

  curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \\n    -d '{"input":"hello"}' \\n    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

  Response: HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout after ~12s repeatedly.

arjun: I can check runtime pools. Fingers crossed it’s not model serving OOM. Giving me a minute to pull pod metrics.

maria: Jin — can you pull the 5xx heatmap and traces for that time window? I suspect a routing layer spike.

jin: grabbing queries. PromQL to examine: 

  sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="ingress",route="/v1/generate",code=~"5.."}[5m])) by (instance)
  sum(rate(nginx_upstream_response_time_bucket[5m]))

  Also querying traces for span name "proxy->model-service": 
  trace.query("span.name:proxy* AND http.path:/v1/generate", start=1915123300, end=1915123620)

  Grafana: <https://grafana.redwood.io/d/ingress/ingress-overview?from=1915123200&to=1915123700>

sre-bot: Alert routed to #oncall-sre. Pager assigned to maria.

maria: Quick checks: 
  - nginx error logs show repeated "upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream" around 14:11-14:16 UTC. Sample: 

```
2026-03-15T14:11:23Z ERROR ingress-nginx controller request_id=xyz upstream: "http://model-service.default.svc.cluster.local:8080" timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.2.3.4, server: api.redwood.ai, request: "POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.1.2.3:8080/generate", host: "api.redwood.ai"
```

maria: Pod side: model-service replicas healthy but connection_accepts spiking and average response_time for some pods at 2.1s median but many tails >10s.

arjun: Looking at container logs for model-service: seeing a small cluster of pods with repeated GC pauses and warnings: "failed to allocate workspace" and a handful of "kv-cache: missing prefix" entries. Pulling the exact logs.

oliver: Customer mentioned they saw some 401s earlier alongside 5xx — might be unrelated token churn. CS supplied tokens that expired though.

cs-elliot: Confirmed: customer tokens rotated at 14:05 UTC then retried many requests. But the 5xx started at ~14:10 and persisted past token rotation window. So likely separate issue.

jin: Tracing results: about ~35% of requests in the window lack any downstream spans (trace gap). Root span exists at the proxy but there’s no model-service span for those traces. Example trace id: trace-0a1b2c, link: <https://jaeger.redwood.ai/trace/trace-0a1b2c>. Correlates with nginx upstream timeouts.

maria: Hypothesis: connection storm to model-service causing queueing + upstream timeouts; some requests hit a pod that was unresponsive (OOM or stuck GC). Need to isolate affected pod IPs and drain.

arjun: I have pod list and metrics. Affected pods: model-svc-5, model-svc-9 show high syscalls and >95% CPU. model-svc-9 logs show repeated: 

```
2026-03-15T14:09:47Z WARN runtime Slow GC pause 12.3s
2026-03-15T14:10:11Z ERROR kv-cache: failed to allocate workspace, falling back to uncached path
```

arjun: Will cordon+drain model-svc-9 and scale up replica count by +2 temporarily (from 6 -> 8) to relieve pressure. Executing: 

  kubectl drain model-svc-9 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n inference
  kubectl scale deploy/model-service -n inference --replicas=8

maria: Do that and watch SLO and 5xx rate. Also enable retry policy at ingress to reduce client-facing 5xx while we remediate: add 2 retries with 1s backoff for route /v1/generate in the gateway config.

platform-pager: Be careful with retries; they can spike load on backend if backend is saturated. If you scale first, then add retries.

arjun: Scaled to 8. model-svc-9 drained. New pods warming up. Initial effect: 5xx rate dropping from 0.9r/s -> 0.12r/s over 2 minutes.

maria: Tracing after drain shows downstream spans returning for previously missing traces. Heatmap tail latency reduced. SLO burn decreased from 4.2 -> 1.1.

support-ops: Customer reports immediate improvement, fewer 504s, still seeing a few timeouts on long requests (>12s).

maria: Follow-ups: 
  - arjun to open ticket for model-service memory tuning and GC investigation.
  - jin to add a dashboard panel for "trace-coverage %" (fraction of proxy spans with downstream spans) and an alert if coverage <90% for 5m.
  - platform to review ingress retry policy and default backoff to avoid amplifying load.

arjun: Created ticket INF-4723: "model-service GC pauses and kv-cache allocation failures" — linking logs and pod IDs.

jin: Added panel draft here: <https://grafana.redwood.io/d/ingress/trace-coverage?panelId=7> — will convert to alert after review.

maria: Also setting a temporary circuit-breaker on the route: if upstream errors > 5% for 1m, fail-fast with 503 to avoid long queuing.

platform-pager: Noted. I'll sync with runtime team tomorrow to discuss safer retry defaults and autoscaling thresholds.

support-ops: Closing loop with customer now. They want postmortem and ETA for permanent fix.

maria: We'll do a short incident summary and a follow-up postmortem. Tagging: @arjun @jin for action items.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-09, severity: medium.

oliver: Thanks all — CS will keep customer updated.

maria: Closing thread here; keeping tickets open for root cause and long-term mitigations. :white_check_mark:
